interpretation.primary: On the preregistered 160-case n=18 screening pool, the frozen learned tail model and the simple v1 gap rule agreed on 159/160 unresolved states. Their only disagreement was a high-confidence model-only continuation (p=0.962, gap65=16) that never beat the incumbent and consumed 519 additional candidate compilations. Thus this targeted test provides no evidence that the current learned model adds decision value beyond the hand-coded v1 gap rule; on the only identified differential case it was strictly worse in compute at equal quality.
interpretation.distribution_shift: The model's probabilities collapsed near zero on most n=18 states despite being trained on n=12/n=14, while one Erdős state received a high false-positive probability. This is evidence of poor or at least unvalidated probability calibration under size shift, not a reason to retune the same pool.
interpretation.selection_scope: Only disagreement tail outcomes were revealed as preregistered; agreement-case futures remain unrevealed in this experiment. Therefore this result compares incremental policy decisions but is not an unbiased estimate of overall challenger-benefit prevalence.
interpretation.next: Freeze the model and disagreement pool. Do not retune. Any next learned continuation model should normalize/remove absolute-scale features, calibrate across n explicitly, and be judged for incremental value over v1 rather than only aggregate gain recovery.
